long_biography.plain_text:
Howard Lorber, the former Vector Group chief executive, met his future business partner Bennett LeBow by chance in a hotel bar. Lorber had studied sociology at Long Island University and worked as a stockbroker and in insurance. He began arranging pension plans and insurance for LeBow, then joined the management of New Valley, the corporate vehicle left after Western Union's sale. The partnership brought him into the business of acquiring and running established companies.

Family history also shaped Lorber's public commitments. His maternal grandparents had left Salonika for the United States before the Holocaust, which destroyed the community they had known. He later travelled there with his sons, visiting the railway station from which Jews had been deported to Auschwitz. He served as chairman of the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum from 2017 to 2021.
